name: Malda Migrator accepted an attacker-supplied Comptroller
summary: Migrator.migrateAllPositions(MigrationParams) reads the source lending protocol out of caller-supplied calldata: _collectMendiPositions calls getAssetsIn(msg.sender) on params.mendiComptroller and then trusts every returned market's balanceOfUnderlying, borrowBalanceStored and underlying, with no check that the comptroller is Mendi's or that the markets are real cTokens. The only allow-list in the contract, allowedMarkets, constrains the destination Malda mToken, not the source. An attacker therefore deployed a fake comptroller and fake cToken markets that report a borrow position against real Malda underlyings, so step 3 made the allow-listed Malda markets lend the underlying to the Migrator via borrowMigration, and step 4 approved the fake market for that amount and called repayBorrowBehalf on it, letting the fake market pull the tokens straight out of the Migrator.

loss.notes: Two-transaction campaign by one sender: the anchor at 19512428:1 and 0x9f12f7b982ffbd90ac5944b3ab8520f7fb5a9882a0a9acf20d63f6922950e59a at 19513198:2. Each component is the exact sum of the underlying that the eight allow-listed Malda mToken markets paid to the Migrator and that the Migrator then forwarded to the attacker EOA 0x370a8db1f020ce70e8eab2502c739844ca2c2910 in those two receipts. Scanning every ERC-20 Transfer whose sender is the Migrator over its entire life shows exactly these two transactions ever routed a market underlying to an address with no code; the other 66 are ordinary Mendi-to-Malda migrations that move funds into Malda markets. Tracking the attacker EOA and both of its exploit contracts to the present shows no further receipts of these underlyings, so nothing was extracted after 19513198 and no recovery is netted here. The attacker also holds mTokens minted against worthless tokens it deployed; those positions were never redeemed for real underlying and are not counted.

ageReset.description: The 5,669-byte Migrator runtime was installed by an inner CREATE in this transaction and is byte-identical at block 19464693 and at block 19512427, the block before the exploit. The contract is not a proxy and has no upgrade or module mechanism.

sources.note: seed-inventory note retained for provenance: onchain review on Linea: the Migrator 0xa0dc62A8eE34bcd7c9a08852C980Ed78E0Cf99c0 was created 2025-05-29 by 0xb819a871d20913839c37f316dc914b0570bfc0ee (Malda deployer), 34.8 hours before the attack tx sent by 0x370a8db1f020ce70e8eab2502c739844ca2c2910; the attack tx is itself a contract-creation deploying the exploit contract 0xb1e2c543035dc0ca845f91aec68f8a891ea5d74f and the fake Comptroller

Reviewed the anchor receipt and call trace, the Etherscan-verified Migrator source on Linea, the creation transaction and its trace, runtime bytecode at deployment and immediately before the exploit, every ERC-20 Transfer the Migrator has ever emitted, and the attacker's full Linea transaction list. The anchor succeeds at 19512428:1 and is a contract creation whose constructor deploys a fake comptroller 0xbc0147742882abcd1aeaf9c0ee5f55333fc81f2b and eight fake cToken markets, then calls the Migrator 0xa0dc62a8ee34bcd7c9a08852c980ed78e0cf99c0 with 0xd9ab05f1, i.e. migrateAllPositions((address,address,address,address)), passing mendiComptroller = the fake comptroller, maldaOperator = the real Operator 0x05bd298c0c3f34b541b42f867baf6707911be437 and userV1 = userV2 = the exploit contract. The Migrator is the callee of a single CALL frame that fans out into 115 direct sub-calls and 1,278 descendants, all in the Migrator's own execution context with no DELEGATECALL, so it is the defect-bearing runtime; the trace shows it calling getAssetsIn (0xabfceffc) on the fake comptroller and then balanceOfUnderlying (0x3af9e669), borrowBalanceStored (0x95dd9193) and underlying (0x6f307dc3) on the fake markets. The verified source confirms _collectMendiPositions takes params.mendiComptroller unvalidated and that allowedMarkets only gates the destination Malda market. Anchor minimality: of the 68 transactions in which the Migrator ever transferred an ERC-20, exactly two sent a market underlying to a code-less address, both from 0x370a8db1f020ce70e8eab2502c739844ca2c2910, at 19512428 and 19513198; the sender's two earlier attempts at 19512205 and 19512251 reverted, so this anchor is the first success. Loss reconstructed from both receipts: USDC 67,041.878203, WETH 17.972421045801780804, USDT 814.451592, WBTC 0.21977997, wstETH 1.446141839628673500, ezETH 23.809031380180695286, weETH 14.913511408838745044 and wrsETH 13.327890405807548875, 282,426.96 USD at contemporaneous DefiLlama prices. Code history: the transaction 0xbdfde437... sent by the Malda deployer EOA 0xb819a871d20913839c37f316dc914b0570bfc0ee at 19464693:4 reaches the Migrator through a CREATE3-style Deployer 0xc781bad08968e324d1b91be3cca30fad86e7bf98, so the immediate CREATE parent recorded as creatorAddress is the ephemeral CREATE2 proxy 0xa701f98fe45d7d3df62420e2427175a5f6038f63. The runtime hashes to 0x86763585b9baf98ab23c0339bcbdf56f8f5aa3b33468571b46d45d52f103fd0c at both block 19464693 and block 19512427, giving a code age of 125,233 s (1.45 days).

notes: deployment.creatorAddress is the ephemeral CREATE2 proxy 0xa701f98fe45d7d3df62420e2427175a5f6038f63 that a CREATE3-style Deployer used to CREATE the Migrator, because that is the immediate creator the execution trace exposes. The transaction was sent by the Malda deployer EOA 0xb819a871d20913839c37f316dc914b0570bfc0ee.
